_about: Catalogue of unsolved historical ciphers not on the Tomokiyo, Schmeh or Dunin lists, plus (since 14 Oct 2026) open items pulled from Cryptoole (research/cryptoole/), some of them on Tomokiyo's list; those carry source "Cryptoole" and their Cryptoole ID in "cryptoole". Scores are 1-5 and unvalidated: importance = historical weight of what the text could add; solvability = odds of a full reading with the material available online; difficulty = technical work needed (1 trivial key alignment, 5 statistics-only on an unknown system). Priority is computed on the page from adjustable weights. Class A = siblings with decipherment in the same volume, B = partial key or known family in print, C = no key, no sibling. seen: image = leaf viewed on the Gallica image; catalogue = selected from the catalogue description only. outcome: 'attempted, open' once an entry has been taken to the leaf here without a reading. Entries read, partly read, resolved or found already in print are removed from this file (19 Sept 2026) and recorded in SOLVED_CATALOGUE.md; ids are not reused. contributed_by: the contributors.json id of an outside contributor who brought the entry in (shown on the page as 'via ...').

entries.title: Nicolas Raince (Rome) to Montmorency and François I, eight letters
entries.correspondents: Nicolas Raince → Montmorency; → François I
entries.status: Attempted 17 Sept 2026 (targets/raince/): Tomokiyo's 1526 key re-measured off his table image and applied glyph by glyph to the 13 May (pp. 29-31) and 20 Nov 1526 (p. 105) passages. Removed from the catalogue when first claimed read in part; restored 23 Oct 2026: Reading audit 22-23 Oct 2026 (George Lasry's test: a reading must build sentences): the passages decode into clauses broken by unresolved stretches in nearly every line, so nothing counts as read. The other letters of the entry carry contemporary interlinear or printed decipherments (Mignet 1886, Bourrilly 1901, DECODE 3696); the open residue is the unglossed part of no. 7 (13 May) and of no. 24 (20 Nov). 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (pull request #163): the 20 Nov residue read, p. 105 lower and the whole of p. 106 (a page of cipher not treated before), about 98% of words with Tomokiyo's table. Entry narrowed: the open residue is the unglossed part of no. 7 (13 May, pp. 29-31).
entries.why: League of Cognac, the Colonna raid on Rome (Sept 1526), prelude to the Sack; Aug 1529 = Cambrai and Bologna.
entries.score_note: Eight letters in presumably one system give enough text for a statistical attack; no key in print that we know of.
entries.verify: Re-read the unresolved glyphs of pp. 29-31 and p. 105 on full-resolution crops; collect the two word signs from the glossed letters nos. 6, 8, 10, 28.
entries.known: Tomokiyo's 1526 key fits after re-measuring (raince.html); the clear close of 13 May transcribed.
entries.open: No. 7 (pp. 29-31) and no. 24 (p. 105), the unglossed lines: unresolved glyphs (~13% of letters) and two word signs absent from Tomokiyo's key; no sentence builds through.

entries.title: Hieronimo Ranzo (?) to 'Garbino', intercepted imperial letter
entries.correspondents: Hieronimo Ranzo (probably; Gattinara's man) → 'Garbino'
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3022 no. 20 (ff. 44r–46v; addition sheet and jargon ff. 48–50v)
entries.status: The other two items first catalogued here (nos. 6 and 10, del Vasto to Charles V) are read: no. 10 by Lasry (2023) with Tomokiyo's edited text, no. 6 in targets/vasto1527/ (its own page since 14 Oct 2026). No. 20 is an Italian letter, Madrid 11 Apr 1528, to 'Garbino', in the same code as Hieronimo Ranzo's letters (fr. 2988). The code is initial letter + number with non-alphabetical numbering; ~3,900 groups are transcribed. The key was recovered from the ciphertext by George Lasry and, independently, by Paolo Rosson (6 Oct 2026; PRs #35, #45), and no. 20 measures 94.4% (targets/ranzo1528/, 18 Oct 2026), just under the read bar. No French decipherment exists; Clair. 327 ff. 279-280 is an undeciphered copy.
entries.why: Five months after the Sack of Rome, during Lautrec's campaign in Italy.
entries.score_note: Large one-part-looking code, one letter, no key; see targets/ranzo1528/NOTES.md.
entries.verify: Look for Ranzo's key or a deciphered Ranzo letter (Simancas, Vienna HHStA) before any statistical attack.
entries.known: No. 6 (del Vasto, Cipher 2) deciphered here with Lasry's key, 98.0% (vasto1527.html); no. 10 (Cipher 1) key recovered by Lasry 2023, read in part with Tomokiyo's text. No. 20: Ranzo's code key recovered from ciphertext only by George Lasry and, independently, Paolo Rosson (6 Oct 2026); no. 20 measured here at 94.4% (ranzo1528.html, PRs #35, #45).
entries.open: No. 20 (Garbino letter): 74 of 1,314 tokens, 27 groups with no value in either key and 47 tentative Lasry values Rosson's key does not confirm; both keys' readings still to be checked against the images of ff. 44r-46v. Blocker: open codes.

entries.title: Espagnol 318 nos. 92, 93, 94: Ferdinand's secretariat ciphers (Great Captain 1500, Suárez de Figueroa 1504, viceroy of Sicily 1503)
entries.correspondents: Lorenzo Suárez de Figueroa (Venice) → the Catholic Monarchs
entries.shelfmark: BnF Espagnol 318 no. 93
entries.folio_note: ff. 118-118v = canvases 446-447
entries.status: Widened again 23 Oct 2026 (Reading audit 22-23 Oct 2026 (George Lasry's test: a reading must build sentences): no. 92 and no. 94 are decoded, not read, so they are back here). Narrowed 21 Oct 2026 to no. 93. The entry first covered five ciphered letters in at least four ciphers: no. 5 (Escrivà's cipher, printed by Parisi 2020; targets/federico1497/), no. 92 (Cifra general, read in part; targets/esp318/) and no. 95 (recto deciphered in full by George Lasry with his CTTS key, PR #75, 22 Oct 2026; verso by Michael Brackx; targets/esp318no95/) have their own entries, and no. 94 (the viceroy of Sicily, Messina 1503) was split off on 21 Oct 2026 after Michael Brackx recovered its key ciphertext-only and read part of its code (issue #62; targets/esp318no94/). No. 93 is unread and its key unknown: code initials exclude Escrivà no. 1 and the Cifra general; a homophonic anneal of 1,016 signs failed (the CVC groups are atomic); no. 94's key does not fit and the two code inventories barely overlap. See targets/esp318no93/.
entries.why: The earliest Spanish diplomatic ciphers online; the Naples war (Cerignola, Garigliano) and Venice 1504.
entries.score_note: Rescored by hand 14 Oct 2026 after the split: no key in hand for either letter; the Gran cifra survives only as Bergenroth's partial list (BNE MSS 20.211/52, not online) and the 'Cifra del visorrey' (BRAH 9/15 ff. 1-6) is unpublished.
entries.verify: Transcribe no. 94 ff. 120r-121v (clear-text islands give context) and test Bergenroth's Gran-cifra list before a cold break.
entries.known: Nothing for nos. 93 and 94: keys not identified; a homophonic anneal of 1,016 signs of no. 93 failed (esp318no93.html). Former siblings: no. 5 printed by Parisi 2020 (federico1497), no. 92 about 75% deciphered with the Cifra general (esp318), no. 95 recto deciphered in full by George Lasry with his own key (esp318no95, PR #75).
entries.open: No. 93 (f. 118r-v) whole letter: CVC nomenclator, the suspected Gran cifra key survives only as Bergenroth's partial list (BNE MSS 20.211/52, not online). No. 92 (targets/esp318/): decoded with the Cifra general (Galende Díaz 1994), not yet built into sentences. No. 94 (targets/esp318no94/): Michael Brackx's key recovered ciphertext-only, about 90 code groups open; his decryption has holes in most sentences.

entries.title: Charles III of Lorraine to the count of Vaudémont, copy
entries.correspondents: Charles III, duke of Lorraine → François, comte de Vaudémont
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3621 no. 97 (fol. 109); no. 22 (fol. 31) is the January decipherment
entries.folio_note: canvas = 2 x folio + 9; no. 97 at fol. 109 = canvas 227, no. 22 at fol. 31 = canvas 71; the folio printed before a piece number belongs to it
entries.status: Attempted 18 Sept 2026 (targets/lorraine1592/, PR #4): the reciprocal letter-pair key recovered from the ciphertext alone (Tomokiyo had broken it in 2025 without publishing a text); no. 22 is a plaintext decipherment of the January letter, with no cipher. Removed from the catalogue when first claimed solved; restored 23 Oct 2026: Reading audit 22-23 Oct 2026 (George Lasry's test: a reading must build sentences): no. 97 decodes into fragments with a gap in almost every line, so nothing counts as read.
entries.why: Lorraine's double game between the League and Henri IV. The ciphered passages carry the military business the clear text only skirts: prisoners and munitions, an order to receive the Duke's commandment and to conserve the plain, Chasteauvillain, and the intention to bring the army back into the quarters of La Fauche, between Neufchateau and Chaumont. The clear text around them has the attempt on Chasteauvillain, munitions promised and undelivered, Chaumont and Buzonville; no. 22's decipherment carries the January business - the Spanish march on Rouen, Mayenne finding the Spaniards resolved on battle, Parma's judgement, then the legate, the Spanish pretensions, Villeroy at Pontoise, the house of Bourbon, Bellievre, and the peace.
entries.score_note: If no. 22's decipherment corresponds to a cipher copy elsewhere in the volume the key falls; otherwise a single copy.
entries.verify: Re-read the 42 per-line crops with the recovered key to correct the barred, dotted and capital variants; ask AD Meurthe-et-Moselle for the ducal key.
entries.known: Letter-pair key recovered from the ciphertext alone (lorraine1592.html).
entries.open: Special signs inside words (about 60 tokens), figures 57, 98, 122, 123, 13, 137, 88, 146, 121, 103, garbled runs L12, L13, L20; no sentence builds. Blocker: no key material; a key or duplicate may survive in the Lorraine ducal archive (AD Meurthe-et-Moselle).

entries.title: Cardinal Sega's legation: the Curia's instruction and a Paris letter
entries.correspondents: the Curia → Cardinal Sega (instruction, duplicate of 14 May 1593); Paris → Rome, 15 May 1593
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3984 nos. 6 (ff. 12-17) and 8 (f. 22r-v)
entries.status: Narrowed 20 Oct 2026 to the two Sega items. The Baudouin-Desportes letters (fr. 3984 f. 186, f. 189) were deciphered by Paolo Rosson on 1 Oct 2026 with Tomokiyo's League key, checked here and written up (targets/desportes1593/, desportes1593.html). The Mauclerc letters (fr. 3983 f. 268, fr. 3984 f. 33, fr. 3985 no. 7 = f. 20) were read at the time: interlinear decipherments, summarised in clear in fr. 3983 f. 140r (targets/mauclerc1593/). Open: no. 8 is a homophonic substitution with a small nomenclator (Z separates words; D, N, X nulls), no. 6 continuous figures (3 and 8 nulls, letters as figure pairs, codes framed by nulls), per Brice Dudout, whose partial candidate readings are at bdudout.github.io/europe-chiffree/en/sega-1593.html. Tomokiyo, Cryptologia 43(1) 2019, gave a preliminary decipherment of 1593 continuous-figure texts, probably including no. 6. Not yet attempted or checked here.
entries.why: The Curia's line on Henri IV's conversion and the Infanta's claim, and a report on the Suresnes conference, May 1593.
entries.score_note: Scores as first assigned to the whole of item 20; narrowed 20 Oct 2026, see targets/sega1593/NOTES.md.
entries.verify: Compare Brice Dudout's readings of nos. 6 and 8 with Tomokiyo, Cryptologia 43(1) 2019; check his no. 8 key on f. 22r-v.
entries.known: Nos. 6 and 8: Brice Dudout described both systems and gives partial candidate readings (bdudout.github.io); Tomokiyo (Cryptologia 43(1) 2019) gave a preliminary decipherment of 1593 figure texts, probably incl. no. 6. Former siblings: Baudouin-Desportes ff. 186, 189 deciphered by Paolo Rosson with Tomokiyo's key (desportes1593.html); Mauclerc letters deciphered at the time (mauclerc1593).
entries.open: No. 8 (f. 22, homophonic with small nomenclator) and no. 6 (ff. 12-17, continuous figures): not attempted or checked here; Dudout's readings still to be compared with Tomokiyo 2019 (sega1593, in progress).

About 950 tokens (Latin letters, digits, ligatures, a few two-digit numbers, clear nulls 'pour', 'car'), transcribed in targets/foix1563/qm_tokens.txt. Since then the sign set was matched to Paul de Foix's own cipher, Tomokiyo's reconstruction from his 1565 letters (Feyseel Nur, PR #21), and Lawrence Beck's independent partial decipherment (PRs #18, #27) agrees with it on 19 of 25 shared signs: deciphered in part, below the read bar.

entries.title: Charles I to Prince Charles, 1 Aug 1648 (cipher passage)
entries.correspondents: Charles I (Carisbrooke) → Charles, Prince of Wales
entries.shelfmark: BL, Harley MS 6988 f 208
entries.status: DECODE R8342 viewed 21 Sept 2026: a clear autograph letter with a 99-group cipher passage (lines 3-8); the King's postscript says the cipher is the one 'sent you by the noble Frend who conveis this Letter'. Printed without the cipher in Halliwell, Letters of the Kings of England ii (1846) 449; ciphertext in Original Letters / cryptiana. The Sept-Nov 1648 Biermann-Bosbach-Brown key and the Titus key are both excluded (targets/charlesi/ NOTES). R8341 (1646) is a graphic-sign key, not this numeric one.
entries.why: The King's secret instruction to his son during the Second Civil War, in a cipher of which no copy is known.
entries.score_note: Reviewed by hand 21 Sept 2026 after viewing the leaf.
entries.verify: Only the key itself would move it: look for the Prince's or Lauderdale's 1648 cipher in the Clarendon, Nicholas (Egerton) or Lauderdale papers.
entries.outcome: attempted, skipped: impossible without the key (no copy known; 59% hapax)
entries.known: Printed without the cipher in Halliwell 1846. The Biermann-Bosbach-Brown 1648 key (which deciphered four other Isle of Wight letters in 2021) and the Titus key are excluded (targets/charlesi, no page).

entries.title: Pandolfo Malatesta, archbishop of Patras, to Gianfrancesco Gonzaga
entries.correspondents: Pandolfo Malatesta (Rome) → Gianfrancesco Gonzaga, lord of Mantua
entries.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Mantova, Archivio Gonzaga (DECODE R1854, image 1)
entries.status: DECODE R1854 image 1 (the record holds four letters in four ciphers; images 2-5 deciphered here, now the entries r1854, mutiliana1428 and cattanei1430; this item is targets/malatesta1428/, split 14 Oct 2026). Three cipher runs, 262 letter-like signs (ſſ, η, ʒ, H, cc, ∩, I, ƀʒ ...) inside a clear Latin letter on the peace of Ferrara (April 1428). Not a simple or homophonic substitution in Latin or Italian (controls pass); the R1853 register's Malatesta keys do not fit.
entries.why: Pandolfo Malatesta's secret plans for his brother-in-law after the peace of Ferrara; one of the oldest unread cipher passages with images online.
entries.score_note: Scored by rule from DECODE metadata (class from key signals, solvability from key, length and language, importance from the correspondents); not yet reviewed by hand.
entries.verify: Pandolfo's 1 March 1438 letter, nearly all in cipher (ASMn AG b. 1081 c. 159-160), survives with its contemporary translation (b. 840 c. 95, printed by Falcioni 2015): if the system is the same, that pair gives the key. Also Falcioni, Quaderni dell'Accademia Fanestre 3 (2004), on Malatesta chancery ciphers.
entries.known: Clear Latin frame read. The other three letters of R1854 deciphered here: image 2 (r1854, key from ciphertext), image 3 (mutiliana1428), images 4-5 (cattanei1430) (malatesta1428.html).
entries.open: The three cipher runs (262 signs): not mono- or homophonic in Latin or Italian; the R1853 Malatesta keys do not fit. Likely key material, Pandolfo's 1438 letter with its translation (ASMn), is not online or printed in cipher.

entries.title: Giuliano Caprile (Eger) to Bonaventura Pistofilo, 9 March 1519
entries.correspondents: Giuliano Caprile → Bonaventura Pistofilo / Alfonso I 'Este
entries.shelfmark: ASMo, Ambasciatori b. 4/23, 1, Envoy reports, Ferrara
entries.status: DECODE R1128: seven lines in Caprile's 1519 two-tier cipher (a small letter over a base sign), no decipherment. Worked 21 Sept and 2 Oct 2026 (targets/caprile1519/, attempted, open: the 1519 tables rebuilt from R1133/7c and R1130/4c give no signal on R1128). The rest of the item is resolved: R1129–R1135 have 1882 decipherments (b/c on Vestigia); the 1520–21 letters (R1136, R1138, R1139) are another cipher, read in part in targets/caprile1520/ (split 14 Oct 2026). Subject, from the clear part and the next letter: Caprile's own lawsuit at Rome. Key obtainable from the 1882 decipherments of nos. 3–8 and 10.
entries.why: A Ferrarese agent at Eger, the Hungarian see held by Ippolito d'Este, writing to Ferrara in 1519–21 on Hungarian affairs on the eve of Mohács.
entries.score_note: Reviewed by hand 19 Sept 2026 from DECODE's metadata and the literature; leaf not viewed.
entries.verify: Apply the archivists' key (ASMo b. 8 fasc. 4) to R1128 after re-attaching upper signs to their bases.
entries.known: R1129-R1135 deciphered in 1882 (Vestigia b/c copies) or interlined. The 1520-21 letters: key recovered from Somogyi 2025's plaintext, V1921 97%, R1139 89.7%, R1136 66.9% (caprile1520.html). R1128 written up as not deciphered (caprile1519.html). The 1519 key was reconstructed by ASMo archivists in the 19th century; sheets printed small in Cremonini 2017, figs. 17.1-17.3 (ASMo Cifrario b. 8 fasc. 4); pointer from Michael Brackx, issue #121.
entries.open: R1128 (9 Mar 1519, seven lines, 183 columns). No outside blocker: the key can be rebuilt from the 1882 sibling decipherments (next step, transcribe R1132 against 6b).

entries.title: Riksarkivet key-box and Oxenstierna ciphers, 8 records (Bremen 1631, R4282, R4306 and Rusdorff 1625 read or partly read and removed)

entries.status: DECODE R4284–R4341, 8 records in four different ciphers, each its own entry since the one-key split of 14 Oct 2026. Viewed 21 Sept 2026. The two Bremen letters of 1631 (R4330–R4331, riksarkivet1628.html) are read and removed from this entry; R4282 was deciphered by George Lasry (decode4282.html). R4306: contributed partial Dutch decipherment by George Lasry, transcribed with CTTS then solved with Opus 5.5 (17 Oct 2026; sweden4306.html, which also records this project's failed attempt of 21 Sept 2026); pencilled 1632? and Amsterdam attribution remain qualified, four code identities open. R4336–R4337 turned out to be Rusdorff's London letters of February 1625 in a homophonic cipher with an alphabetical nomenclator; key recovered from the ciphertext by George Lasry (21 Oct 2026, PR #72; rusdorff1625.html) and removed from this entry. Open: R4284 (Latin 1628, Camerarius docket; riksarkivet4284.html) — attacked with Latin annealing and against two box keys, not broken; R4333–R4335 (Rusdorff → Oxenstierna 1628, another cipher; rusdorff1628.html) and R4338–R4341 (E 708, Swedish, June 1633, not 1646; glossed in part at the time; oxenstierna1633.html) surveyed only.

entries.title: Gerard Carel baron van Spaen tot Voorstonden, envoy of the King of Holland (Düsseldorf), to Maarten van der Goes, minister of foreign affairs, 14 and 15 Jan 1808
entries.correspondents: G. C. van Spaen tot Voorstonden, envoy of the King of Holland → Maarten van der Goes (1751-1826), minister of foreign affairs
entries.shelfmark: NA The Hague, 02.01.08., Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken, 1796-1810, inv. nr. 281
entries.status: DECODE R1941, viewed 21 Sept 2026 (targets/spaen1808/). Two items: the letter of 14 Jan 1808 (228 groups) and an annex of 15 Jan (75 groups; DECODE images P1 and P2 are two photos of the same page). Plain numerical code, groups 15-1339, no marks, dashes as separators; clear openings and closings in Dutch. No decipherment on the images, and DECODE holds no key for it (the 1798 and 1803 Croiset books R1891/R1035 do not fit). DECODE's 'annex solved' has no reading attached to the record. Not in Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken V (searched). 303 groups, 222 distinct, from a code of 1,300+ entries: not breakable without the key. NA inventory: inv. 281 = letters of J.F.G. van Spaen and G. van Riemsdijk, commissioners for the takeover of the ceded districts (Lijmers, Huissen, Malburgen, Zevenaar), 1806-09; Düsseldorf = Grand Duchy of Berg, not Westphalia. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): dated Düsseldorf, 12 January 1808 (No. 4); 14 January is the date of receipt ('Exh'). Two-part code, not breakable without a crib.

entries.title: Florence, letters to the Signoria in the cipher of 1414 (Gabbrielli's partial key, letters never read)
entries.correspondents: unknown Florentine envoy or commissary → Signoria / Dieci di Balìa
entries.shelfmark: ASF, Signori, Responsive originali, filza 1 (key: ASF Chiavi delle cifre II, pars 3 no. 1)
entries.status: Meister 1902 p. 49 prints "Florenz, Beispiele 1: Cifra Decemviri di Balia 1414 (Lettere della Signoria risponsive; filza Nr. 1)", a partial homophonic alphabet Gabbrielli rebuilt in 1864 from glossed words (several letters blank; per = 8, et = f, che = dum). No sender or folio given; no reading of the letters printed (Guasti's Commissioni has nothing for 1414). The same situation as florence1429, where Gabbrielli's 1424 table read only glossed words. Session of 23 Sept 2026 (targets/florence1414/): key transcribed (KEY.md, 38 signs); 'filza 1' is an old number (today's Signori Responsive 1 is 1340), so the letters are probably in Signori Responsive 7-8 or Signori-Dieci-Otto, Legazioni e commissarie, missive e responsive 8; not on DECODE, Yale Ilardi reels or ASF PAD. Outgoing registers Legazioni e commissarie 5-6 (PAD) scanned: clear, no cipher; reg. 6 ff. ~35-52 are the 1414 instructions (candidate senders).
entries.why: The oldest Florentine cipher letters; a full reading would beat the project's 1425 record by eleven years.
entries.verify: Order from ASF: Gabbrielli vol. II pars 3 no. 1 (key page with his list of letters used) and the vol. II index, then the letters (likely Signori Responsive 7-8 or Legazioni e commissarie, missive e responsive 8). Then read as in florence1429.
entries.outcome: attempted, open: blocked, no image of the letters online (23 Sept 2026, targets/florence1414/)
entries.known: Gabbrielli's 1864 partial key (printed by Meister 1902, p. 49) transcribed here as 38 signs (florence1414). No reading of any of the letters has been found.
entries.open: The 1414 letters themselves: not located or imaged (probably ASF Signori Responsive 7-8 or Legazioni e commissarie 8); not on DECODE, Ilardi reels or ASF PAD. Blocker: needs ASF photographs.

entries.title: Siena, "Lettere in cifra" of the Concistoro: the pieces still unsolved (nos. 4, 7, 14, 15, 19, 21; no. 1 of 1421 unphotographed)
entries.correspondents: Sienese envoys and others → the Concistoro of Siena
entries.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Siena, Concistoro 2308, fasc. 2 "Lettere in cifra": nos. 7, 19, 21 (R4796, R4807, R4809); no. 1 (1421), 2, 26-28 (not on DECODE)
entries.status: Narrowed 18 Oct 2026 to the pieces still unsolved, after George Lasry's report of 17 Oct 2026 (one entry per key; index research/siena2308/). Open: no. 7 (R4796, orator at Milan to the Balia, 1450s; 363 signs, interlinear gloss gives nine values; filed key R4750 and five others fail it; targets/siena7/), no. 19 (R4807, Sienese envoys, 9 March, 1440s; 118 signs; targets/siena19/), no. 21 (R4809, 'Karissimo come padre', 15th c.; 107 signs; targets/siena21/): attempted, too short without a key. No. 1 (1421) and nos. 2, 26-28 are not among the DECODE photographs (needs ASSi). The other pieces are deciphered on their own entries: nos. 20/23, 12, 6/24, 25, 11, 18, 17, 5?, 9, 13/16, 10 and 8 (no. 8 from the contemporary decipherment on its sheet, aligned here 18 Oct 2026). 23 Oct 2026, Reading audit 22-23 Oct 2026 (George Lasry's test: a reading must build sentences): no. 4 (R4793, Borghesi 1456; targets/borghesi1456/), no. 14 (R4802; targets/siena14/) and no. 15 (R4803; targets/siena15/) are decoded, not read, and are back among the open pieces.
entries.why: Nos. 7, 19 and 21 are the last undeciphered 15th-century pieces of the Sienese file. No. 1 (1421) would not be its oldest letter: George Lasry's decipherments include letters of March and April 1413 (nos. 12, 20, 23; the years reconstructed, not written).
entries.verify: Order nos. 1, 2, 26-28 from ASSi; for nos. 7, 19, 21 look for a sibling letter in the same key or a fresh transcription in CTTS (no. 7: rerun with the gloss values fixed).
entries.known: Every other photographed piece is deciphered on its own entry (index: siena1421.html). George Lasry recovered the keys of no. 12, 10 March 1413 (the year reconstructed from the sixth indiction and the context), nos. 20 and 23, 30 March and about April 1413 (years inferred), nos. 6/24, 9, 11, 13/16, 17, R4794 and no. 15 in part; this project recovered nos. 4, 18, 25 and no. 14 in part; nos. 8 and 10 were deciphered at the time. No. 7: the interlinear gloss gives nine values.
entries.open: Nos. 7 (R4796, 363 signs), 19 (R4807, 118) and 21 (R4809, 107): no key; none of the filed keys fits, and neither George Lasry nor this project has deciphered them. No. 1 (Meister's 1421 letter), 2 and 26-28 are not photographed; they need the Archivio di Stato di Siena. No. 4 (R4793, 144 signs): key rebuilt from an alphabet fragment and the glosses, 114 signs given a value, no sentences. No. 14 (R4802): key recovered from the ciphertext alone, L01-L26 decoded, not read. No. 15 (R4803): partly deciphered by George Lasry by crib guessing (no key filed), decoded, not read.

entries.title: Military news for Prince Carl August Friedrich of Waldeck, in a three-digit code
entries.correspondents: unknown informant → Prince Carl August Friedrich of Waldeck
entries.shelfmark: Hessisches Staatsarchiv Marburg, HStAM 118 a Nr. 3954, ff. 3-4 (HCPortal record 517)
entries.status: Attempted 28 Sept 2026 (targets/waldeck1744/): 717 groups, 303 distinct, transcribed. The prince's French draft reply on f. 4v answers a letter of 18 January (1744). Probably a two-part homophonic nomenclator (7/90/924 homophones; no alphabetical, column or multiplicative numbering fits); synthetic controls of that design show the key is not identifiable from one letter. No key on Arcinsys, HCPortal or DECODE; the undigitised 118 a Nr. 1973-1980 (Feldzug 1744) may hold the key or a deciphered copy.
entries.why: War of the Austrian Succession; Waldeck commanded Dutch troops. A hard code with no known key.
entries.verify: Look for further reports in the same code in HStAM 118 a (Waldeck papers) before attempting; one page of code is thin.
entries.known: Nothing deciphered. 717 groups transcribed 28 Sept 2026; dated 18 Jan 1744 from the prince's draft reply on f. 4v (waldeck1744).
entries.open: The whole letter: not deciphered. Two-part nomenclator with no key on Arcinsys, HCPortal or DECODE; synthetic controls show one letter is too little to rebuild it; possible key or copy in undigitised HStAM 118 a Nr. 1973-1980.

entries.status: Cryptoole XX1654-1 (open). Cryptiana unsolved.htm and louisxiv0.htm ('Prince of Condé (1654-1655)'): the 1654 letter f. 98 seems undeciphered and in a different cipher from the known 1655 Condé–Barrière cipher (f. 108); whether f. 101 reads with the 1655 key is untested. DECODE R8395/R8398: Thurloe papers volume, clear text in English and French, images by login. Copies of Condé–Barrière letters (partly cipher) are also in Bodleian MS. Rawl. A (Thurloe papers). Reviewed 20 Oct 2026: R8395 is Barrière to Condé, as the manuscript heading/source list state; R8398 is the reverse direction. Both images and R8405/R8406 key images retrieved. No validated diacritic-preserving reading established.
entries.why: Condé, in Spanish service after the Fronde, courting Cromwell through his London agent in the year of the Anglo-French rapprochement; Thurloe intercepted the letter.
entries.verify: Download R8395 and R8398 with the DECODE cookie (targets/bordeaux) and transcribe them. Test f. 101 against the 1655 key (R8405/R8406). Look for a deciphered or clear copy of the 15 Sept 1654 letter in Thurloe State Papers vol. ii and Bodleian MS. Rawl. A (Thurloe) before attacking f. 98 ciphertext-only.
entries.known: The 1655 Condé-Barrière cipher (f. 108, key R8405/R8406) is known. 20 Oct 2026: R8395 shown to be Barrière to Condé (R8398 the reverse); images and key photographs retrieved. No reading of either piece.
entries.open: f. 98 (R8395, 15 Sept 1654, apparently another cipher) and f. 101 (R8398, 18 June 1655): not deciphered; f. 101 not yet tested with the 1655 key; diacritics need transcribing first.

entries.status: Cryptoole XX1678-1 (open). Attempted 27 Oct 2026, not solved (targets/ormond1678/). 20 figures, all distinct: 445 and 342 before two runs ('726 91 33 425 93 58 384 54 700 720' and '732 573 526 32 643 214 55 440'). The sixth figure of run 1 is printed 58 on the p. 93 scan; '57' came from Tomokiyo's quotation. The calendar gives no gloss. The 1678 Ormond-Arran code of Arran's 9 Feb letter (pp. 105-106) is a two-letter code, so it cannot be this one. The Ormond-Longford 1680 key puts the low figures on bare consonants (l, k, m, h), as in Tomokiyo's rejected trial. Too short and repeat-free for a ciphertext-only attack.
entries.why: Ormond testing his son with a family cipher in the Popish-Plot year; small, but from a well-documented family of reconstructed Ormond keys.
entries.verify: Have NLI MSS 2335-2362 searched for the 24 Jan 1677/8 letter, and Bodleian Carte 216-217 for Arran's copy as received; look for an interlinear decipherment or a numeric Ormond-Arran key of 1677-78. Ormond-Anglesey 1663 and Ormond-Longford 2-3 are untested.
entries.known: Nothing deciphered. The passage (20 numbers, count corrected 20 Oct 2026) is printed in HMC Ormonde n.s. iv p. 93 without gloss; Tomokiyo's trial with the Ormond-Longford key was rejected.
entries.open: All 20 numbers: not deciphered; the 1678 Ormond-Arran code is not rebuilt and the manuscript (Ormonde papers, NLI) is unlocated; very short.

entries.status: Cryptoole XX1718-2 (open). DECODE R10181 'Non-decrypted', public access. Attempted 28 Oct 2026 (targets/duran1718/): 317 groups, 149 distinct, values 2-768 (one 877); NoAutopilot's transcription checked on the images and its missing last line of f2v added. All nine legation keys R10189-R10197 (Cajón 19 leg. 30, 1711-1718) tested: none covers the range (112 groups above 530) and R10194 gives nonsense on the in-range groups. Brice Dudout (email, 27 Oct 2026) suggested an alphabetical word code of about 880 entries ('de' 163, 'del' 164, 'que' 652); a one-part ciphertext-only annealer (control 49-60% of tokens, function words only) gave word salad ascending, descending and with those anchors fixed. Blocked on the key.
entries.why: A war-office despatch to Spain's envoy at Genoa three months after Cape Passaro, during Alberoni's war with the Quadruple Alliance, kept in the legation's own archive with its key sheets.
entries.verify: Find the 1718 war-office code: ACA Diversos, Legación en Génova y Turín, Cajón 19 leg. 30 docs 4, 7, 9-14, 17, 18 (not on DECODE); AGS Guerra Moderna / Estado; or San Felipe's deciphered register at Genoa.

entries.title: Fragments in Girolamo Sirtori's cipher broken by Luis Valle de la Cerda (BNE Mss/994)
entries.correspondents: unknown writer using Girolamo Sirtori's cipher; handed to Luis Valle de la Cerda by a secretary of the Council of State
entries.shelfmark: Madrid, Biblioteca Nacional, Mss/994, ff. 83-90 (ciphertext ff. 85-87); BDH bdh0000174344
entries.status: Cryptoole ITXXXX-1 (partly solved). Valle broke it and said he had devised the same scheme fifteen years earlier; his solution is not extant. Transcription by Sara Gómez Hernández; partial Latin reading by Eloy Caballero (2012) on Cipher Mysteries. Review 20 Oct 2026: Caballero explicitly presents a tentative interpretation with unspecified abbreviation expansions and acknowledges excess freedom. Its Latin reading is unverified; it is not accepted here as a recovered deterministic key or a verified partial solution. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): the episode is Valladolid 1604, not 1599 (as Cryptiana noted). Valle never says he broke these letters: he says he already had 'la misma' cipher, shown to Philip II fifteen years earlier. The ciphertext is two real letters, to Andrés de Prada (f. 85r) and to Juan Baptista de Tassis (ff. 86r-86v), so Spanish or Italian rather than Latin. Unread; the BDH images (140 ppi) are too coarse, and he has asked the BNE for high-resolution scans.
entries.why: Sirtori's own cipher, and a test of the claim by Spain's cipher secretary that he had anticipated it.
entries.verify: Download ff. 83-90 from BDH, re-transcribe keeping the abbreviation marks, and test Caballero's partial key against a Latin (and Italian/Spanish) model; read ff. 83-84 and 88-90 for Valle's own description of the scheme.
entries.known: Broken at the time by Luis Valle de la Cerda (his solution not extant). Transcription by Sara Gómez Hernández; Eloy Caballero's tentative partial Latin reading (2012, Cipher Mysteries) is unverified and not accepted here.
entries.open: The ciphertext of ff. 85-87 (~800 characters): no verified decipherment or key; needs a fresh transcription keeping the abbreviation marks.

entries.status: Attempted 26 Oct 2026 (ferdinand1634), closed unread: no image of the letter is online or in print. Mírka (2012, n. 37-39, 135): a contemporary copy, the only enciphered one among the copies of Ferdinand's letters to Trauttmansdorff; a clear note at the end says Ferdinand enciphered it and sent it by his own messenger; cipher alphabet of two- and three-digit numbers only (nomenclator with homophones, bigrams, probably codes). entries.why: A ciphered letter from the victor of Nördlingen to the Emperor's chief negotiator in November 1634, during the Pirna talks that led to the Peace of Prague.
entries.verify: Order scans of kart. 6, inv. č. 68 from SOA Plzeň (Klášter). Mírka (n. 38) suggests the key may be in Vienna (FA Trauttmansdorff, HHStA). Not the R1887 system of 28 Oct 1634 (graphic signs + three-letter codes, ferdinand3).
entries.known: Mírka 2012 describes a numerical nomenclator (two- and three-digit numbers) that he could not break. Ferdinand's graphic-sign cipher of 28 Oct 1634 (R1887, ferdinand3) is a different system.
entries.open: The whole letter: not seen; no image online, on DECODE or in Mírka's article; scans needed from SOA Plzeň.

entries.title: Undeciphered figures printed in the Mémoires et correspondance de Duplessis-Mornay (1824): Loménie 1595, Duplessis 1597-98 (the 1593 Du Maurier/Serviez figures are read)
entries.correspondents: Du Maurier, J. de Serviez, Loménie → Philippe Duplessis-Mornay; Duplessis-Mornay → various
entries.shelfmark: Mémoires et correspondance de Duplessis-Mornay (Paris 1824-25) vol. 5 pp. 471-475, 487-488; vol. 6 pp. 179-181; vols. 7-8 (archive.org mmoiresetcorre05morn etc.)
entries.folio_note: 1593: 8 passages, 93 groups (targets/mornay1593/ciphertext.txt). Mme de Rohan 1594 (vol. 6 LVI) is printed with its decipherment, a key for the household.
entries.source: Printed edition (found during the Archives nationales sweep, 25 Oct 2026)
entries.status: The 1824 editors printed these figures because they had no key (vol. 6 p. 82 n. 1). Web search found no later decipherment. Attempted 25 Oct 2026: two-letters-per-group anneal failed (targets/mornay1593/). Originals possibly AN 402AP or Institut Mornay papers. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): the 1593 figures read (folded alphabet; our two-letters-per-group hypothesis, credited); Du Maurier's letter is Tuesday 20 July 1593, not June. Entry narrowed to the 1595-98 figures.
entries.why: Henri IV's conversion summer of 1593 seen from Duplessis-Mornay's correspondents; no archive request needed, page images online, and a sibling key (Rohan 1594) in the same edition.
entries.verify: Transcribe the 1597-98 figures (vols. 7-8); test the Rohan 1594 key and variants of the folded 1593 key on Loménie 1595 and Duplessis 1597.
entries.known: Rohan 1594 letter deciphered in print. The 1593 Du Maurier and Serviez figures (vol. 5, 93 groups) read by Brice Dudout, 27 Oct 2026: two letters per group on a folded alphabet (a 2, c-m odd 5-21 rising, n-u even 22-8 falling); applied here to the project's transcription, 93/93 groups (targets/mornay1593/).
entries.open: Loménie 24 Feb 1595 and Duplessis Jan 1597 (transcribed, a different system; the Rohan key does not fit); later 1597 and 1598 figures in vols. 7-8 not transcribed.
entries.score_note: Scored by hand 25 Oct 2026 from the printed pages.

entries.title: Antoni Augustyn Deboli → King Stanisław August, cipher despatches from St Petersburg, 1788 (older-code despatches)
entries.correspondents: Antoni Augustyn Deboli (Polish envoy at St Petersburg) → Stanisław August
entries.language: Polish/French (unknown which; the clear despatches of the same days are in Polish)
entries.shelfmark: AGAD Warszawa, Zbiór Popielów (zesp. 12), sygn. 428
entries.folio_note: 111 cipher despatches, 4 Jan-26 Dec 1788
entries.status: AGAD inventory: "Korespondencja polityczna tajna (pismo cyfrowe) ... Listy zapisane szyfrem"; no decipherment noted. Keys in the same fonds: ZbPop 444 "Cyfra polska posłana do Petersburga Deboliemu" 8 III 1783; 451 "Chiffre François Nouveau envoyé a Monsieur Deboli" 1780; 453-454 the Cabinet's numbered keys 1772-1795 (not seen online). Not on DECODE (list dump searched); not in repo (known.py Deboli, Popiel: no hits). Scans online on AGAD's own image server. 27 Oct 2026 (targets/deboli1790/): attempted. The 1788 volume uses two codes. From the spring, despatches begin with 4000 and use the 1789-91 Polish code; their decipherments are the same-date Polish texts in ZbPop 417 (20 May pair aligned: 360 = o, 1657 = z). The earlier despatches are in an older code (groups to about 2450). ZbPop 417 has same-date copies for them too, but the 11 Jan pair did not align on its opening lines (homophones likely). Open: the older-code despatches, Jan to spring 1788 (and the older-code parts of later ones).

entries.title: Anhalt-Dessau agents in Prague → Prince Johann Georg I: Johann von Alairt's letters of 1610-11 in upside-down German, deciphered at the time except a slip of Nov 1611; the prince's cipher table and a slip key are unused
entries.correspondents: Johann Loew; "Johann von Alairt"; Jacob Quelwitz → Johann Georg I of Anhalt-Dessau / Peter Meyer
entries.shelfmark: Landesarchiv Sachsen-Anhalt, Z 44 (Abteilung Dessau) A 9a Ic Nr. 1 Bd. I-III, Nr. 2 Bd. I-IV, Nr. 3, Nr. 4 Bd. I, Nr. 5, Nr. 6 (all digitised)
entries.folio_note: Images: https://recherche.landesarchiv.sachsen-anhalt.de/images//Z_44/A_9a_Ic_<volume>/max/Z_44__A_9a_Ic_<volume>__NNNN.jpg (e.g. Nr_2_Bd_I). Keys: Nr. 2 Bd. I image 6, 'Cifra ... Joannis Georgii Principis Anhalt', a sign alphabet a-z and a nomenclator 10-70; Nr. 2 Bd. II image 184, a slip with signs for 11 names and words (37 = Iudaeus, 68 = Einsidell). Alairt's letters from Prague with cipher, deciphered between the lines: Nr. 1 Bd. II images 152-153 (5 Apr 1610), 177 (19 Apr), 197 (4 May), 241-242 (18 May); Nr. 1 Bd. III images 41-42 (May), 154 (July), 263 (Aug). Undeciphered: Nr. 4 Bd. I image 400, an 8-line slip docketed 'praes. Dessau den 23. Novemb. 1611'.
entries.status: Checked image by image by Michael Brackx (issue #128, 27 Oct 2026); images 6, 241 and 400 confirmed here. The cipher in use is Alairt's: German in Latin script with every letter turned top to bottom (b/p, d/q, n/u, m/w trade places; e looks like o). Every cipher line of his 1610 letters has a decipherment in a second hand above it, except formulas. The Nov 1611 slip has none; its first line reads 'Will der Kayser bericht werden, dass der Hertz[og] von Braun[schweig] ...' (Brackx; agreed here). No letter in Nr. 1 Bd. I-III, Nr. 2 Bd. I-II, Nr. 3 or Nr. 4 Bd. I uses the prince's table or the slip key. Not searched: Nr. 2 Bd. III-IV (accounts), Nr. 5-6 (newsletters), Nr. 1 Bd. III image 80 (would not load). Christian I of Anhalt-Bernburg's cipher systems 1608-27 are in Z 18 A 9a Nr. 1/0. Target folder: targets/anhalt1610/ (in progress).
entries.why: Intelligence from Rudolf II's Prague for the Calvinist Anhalt princes before the Union.
entries.score_note: Rescored 27 Oct 2026 after Michael Brackx's check (issue #128): the system is known and the 1610 letters are deciphered at the time; the 1611 slip is the open piece.
entries.verify: Read the Nov 1611 slip (Nr. 4 Bd. I image 400) by reflecting it top to bottom; check the 1610 decipherments against the cipher lines. Search Nr. 2 Bd. III-IV and Nr. 5-6 for letters in the prince's table.

entries.title: French consular dispatches in cipher to Talleyrand captured on the ship Astrea (the Gibraltar packet)
entries.correspondents: J. A. B. Rozier (former French vice consul at New York) → Talleyrand
entries.place: United States → Paris (captured at sea; sent on by US consul John Gavino, Gibraltar)
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Miscellaneous Letters of the Department of State (M179 roll 17): John Adams to Timothy Pickering, Quincy, 1 Apr 1799 (naId 55028996), the cover letter; the location of the ciphered packet itself (originals and the Adams copies by Thomas B. Adams and William Shaw) is not established
entries.folio_note: Adams's cover letter is not digitised in the catalogue; the packet held at least two letters from Rozier (Brumaire and Frimaire an VII) plus others; length unknown
entries.status: NARA item description: Adams submits 'a packet of papers sent by the United States Consul at Gibraltar, but they have not been deciphered'. Adams's letter (Founders Online) says no one in Boston would undertake them and James Lovell 'despairs of being able to make a key'. Pickering to Hamilton 18 Jun 1799: Rozier showed his cipher and Pickering checked some coded passages against Rozier's plain copies. So the Rozier letters were checked in part with the writer's own key; the other letters in the packet and a full decipherment are not recorded. Not on DECODE; not in the repo. 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #110; targets/astrea1799/, in progress): the editors name only the two Rozier letters as in code (no. 1, 27 Oct 1798; no. 2, 22 Nov 1798 with a postscript of 23 Nov and an extract of Rozier to Hédouville of 20 Nov). Pickering's check-reading (PAH 23:199-200) is a summary only; no decipherment in print. Adams Papers microfilm reel 393 at MHS (slip 100399, 32 p.) holds the packet or the Adams copies.
entries.why: French consular reporting to Talleyrand at the height of the Quasi-War, read by the Adams administration only through the writer's own selective key demonstration.

Still unbroken: EHNPZ 123 (8 Jul, net 4fc), AFUVO 26, ZUBZE 8, MZXNX 21, AAXYN 31, AOXST 91; also BCUCC Nr. 20 NF (5 Sep 1941), not in this row. See targets/ts1941pz6/ (WAINUT, PR #125; ciphertext-only attempt failed; Status: no write-up). Not in the repo (only Enigma rows of this collection are on HCPortal; Cryptoole's CryptoCellar rows were dropped wholesale as Enigma). This entry covers all 30 unbroken 1941 Truppenschlüssel messages on the CryptoCellar list, by net: net 'pz6', 4 July 1941 (Nr. 88, 90, 91, 92, 94, 97; also 95, 96 same day); net 'nfw', 3 July 1941 (Nr. 84, 85, 86); net '4fc', 8 July 1941 (Nr. 123, 129, 130); net 'f8y', 6 and 8 July 1941 (Nr. 109, 110, 121); net '8be', 25 July 1941 (Nr. 263, 264); June-September 1941 (VHRNE Nr. 284, AOXST Nr. 91, XWFEC Nr. 193, MZXNX Nr. 21, AAXYN Nr. 31, DOLHA Nr. 252, LSSLG Nr. 268, ZUBZE Nr. 8, CFQIB Nr. 281, YSGSS Nr. 56, AFUVO Nr. 26). entries.title: Delacroix (French Foreign Minister) → Létombe (French consul general, Philadelphia), despatch No. 5 entirely in a French numeric code, copy sent by Rufus King
entries.correspondents: Charles Delacroix → Philippe de Létombe (copy forwarded by Rufus King to Timothy Pickering)
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Great Britain, vol. 5 (10 Aug 1796-28 Dec 1797) = microfilm M30 roll 4 (image path M30-004), catalog naId 188512917
entries.folio_note: frames 0244 right, 0245 left and right (0244 left blank): 653 code groups, values 2-1198, 297 distinct, in a clerk's copy marked 'Dup.', '(Copy)', 'No. 5 Duplicata'; heading and close in clear, signed 'Ch. Delacroix'; catchwords (806, 278) at the page feet confirm no group lost between pages. King's covering No. 53 ends on frame 0243.
entries.status: Transcribed in full by Michael Brackx (issue #122, 27 Oct 2026; transcription in the issue). King's No. 53: 'I have no means of decyphering it'; no decipherment on frames 0236-0252. Turner, Correspondence of the French Ministers 1791-1797 (AHA 1903) does not print No. 5, but prints Létombe's reply No. 42 (22 Brumaire an VI, p. 1077, from the ministry's decipherment, CP États-Unis 48 f. 355): he will follow what the 25 Messidor despatch prescribed for keeping his political correspondence, 'dont je dicte moi-même les chiffres'. So part of No. 5 is probably about the keeping and ciphering of his political letters. Statistics: repeats 705 806 711/400 405 ×7, 474 670 1068 ×3; adjacent frequent pairs 972/973 and 81/82 hint at a one-part code, but a one-part word anneal did not converge; flat profile (top ten 14%). Not on DECODE.
entries.why: A Directory instruction to the French chargé/consul general in Philadelphia days before Delacroix left office and on the eve of the XYZ mission, which Rufus King obtained in London (probably from Grenville's decipherers); its content is not known from the US side.
entries.verify: Find the clear minute of 25 Messidor an V in AMAE CP États-Unis 47 or 48, or Nasatir & Monell's calendar (1967). Alternatively, find Létombe's 1797-98 ciphered despatches with the ministry's decipherments (CP États-Unis 48; Turner prints them from the decipherment) to rebuild the code.

entries.title: Soviet and German cipher radiograms of 1921 (Moscow ↔ Berlin, Stockholm, Christiania, Kharkov), intercepted at Constantinople by the US High Commission and never deciphered
entries.correspondents: Chicherin / Narkomindel Moscow ↔ Soviet representation Berlin (Kopp, Krestinsky, 'Polpred'), Stockholm, Christiania, Reval; Nikolaev → Kharkov; Auswärtiges Amt Berlin ↔ Deutsche Vertretung Moskau (Hilger); copies sent by Admiral Mark L. Bristol, US High Commissioner, Constantinople
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Central Decimal File 1910-29, 861.00 (Political Affairs, Russia), microfilm M316 rolls 40-48 (RG 64 digital copies): file units naId 604700562 (861.00/8376-8492, Mar 1921), 604701877 (8493-8622, Apr), 604703234 (8623-8773, May-Jun), 604704577 (8774-8910, Jun-Jul), 604705830 (8911-9012, Jul-Sep), 604707113 (9013-9064, Sep-Oct), 604708415 (9065-9159, Oct-Nov), 604709981 (9160-9240, Nov-Dec), 604711297 (9241-9329, Dec 1921-Feb 1922); the War Department copies are RG 457, Archival and Historian's Source Files, 6707N 'Russian Coded Messages, 1921 (Provided by U.S. High Commissioner Constantinople)' (naId 23890165, not digitised)
entries.folio_note: Typed copies of intercepted radiograms, one per frame with date, route and addresses (e.g. 'MARCH 22d 1921 FROM ... TO MOSCOW 71915 67404 33684 ...'; 'SEPTEMBER 4th 1921 FROM BERLIN TO MOSCOW SCHITSCHERIN MOSKAU FUNKSPRUCH'; 'SEPTEMBER 28th 1921 FROM MOSCOW TO BERLIN POLPRED BERLIN'), mostly 4- and 5-figure groups. Frames with cipher text by roll (OCR count): M316-040 0889-0893 (5); 041 0543-1068 (61); 042 0244-1276 (83); 043 0427-1204 (42); 044 0186-1073 (56); 045 0048-0638 (22); 046 0178-1178 (45); 047 0155-1070 (64); 048 0128-0766 (13): about 390 frames, about 62,000 groups. Covering despatches: 861.00/8575 (Bristol No. 153, 20 Apr 1921, M316-041-0871: the Russian intercept operator's notes on the traffic), 040-0888 (March 1921: hopes anti-Bolshevik Russians may help find the key; Col. Castle sending similar messages to the War Department), 043-0936 (July 1921: 'unable to report any progress regarding the deciphering of the code messages of the Bolshevik Government'); 9071, 9130, 9132, 9133 (Oct-Nov 1921, Moscow-Berlin and Moscow-Christiania). M316-041-1073 'Deciphered telegrams of Soviet authorities' (Petrograd-Reval) is a separate, small set in clear.
entries.status: Unblocked 27 Oct 2026 (NARA slice L, research/nara_triage_l/): the purport list (naId 87657409) led to the 861.00 file, which is filmed on M316 and digitised as RG 64 copies; all nine 1921 rolls fetched and the OCR read. The High Commission could not decipher the traffic and the Department records no decipherment; the War Department (MI-8) received parallel copies (RG 457 6707N). Some of the same Soviet traffic may have been read by GC&CS (HW 12, 1921) and the German side is Auswärtiges Amt traffic; neither has been checked. Distinct from 710 (Chicherin → Sukhanov 1918).
entries.why: A large, dated corpus of early Soviet and German diplomatic cipher radio traffic from 1921, filed as typed copies with the intercept operator's notes: the Rapallo-era Moscow-Berlin channel, unread by the Americans who collected it.
entries.verify: View sample frames (M316-041-0543, 0871; 046-0178); separate the Russian and German systems by route and group length; check HW 12 (GC&CS) 1921 Soviet decrypts and the RG 457 4896 worksheets for keys or matching texts; compare with TICOM 1036 on early Soviet systems.

entries.title: The "Tampico message": Riverbank reports it cannot solve it, 1917
entries.correspondents: unknown sender at Tampico (German agent traffic presumed) / Riverbank Laboratories (Fabyan, Friedman) → War College Division / MIS
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 165, War College Division general correspondence, file 10020-60 (27 Aug 1917; NARA microfilm M1024); indexed in M912 (Name Index, roll 34, frame 0947, naId 221122451)
entries.folio_note: Index card entries 10020-41 to 10020-64 (July-Sept 1917): "repts. re inability to solve Tampico message" (10020-60); "fwds. monthly report of Sept. 1-17 undeciphered messages" (10020-64); "fwds two cipher code messages to be translated" (10020-61).
entries.status: The M912 index card (OCR of frame 0947) shows Riverbank reporting that it could not solve a message from Tampico, and sending monthly lists of undeciphered messages. The M1024 roll for files 10018-10049 (roll 310, naIds 267255625 + 267257126) was fetched and searched: frame 0051 is a withdrawal card, "File 10020 ... Transferred to: Military Information Division", so the file is in the MID correspondence (RG 165 entry 65), which is not digitised. 27 Oct 2026 (targets/tampico1917/): attempted; known only from the M912 index card (roll 34 frame 0947): "repts. re inability to solve Tampico message" (10020-60), with 10020-61 and 10020-64 (undeciphered messages, Sept 1917) beside it. The file itself is not scanned. Order RG 165 10020-60 to -64.
entries.why: Tampico was the centre of German agent activity against the Mexican oil fields in 1917; the message and the "undeciphered messages" reports are a list of what Friedman's first unit could not break.
entries.verify: Order MID file 10020 (RG 165 entry 65, MID correspondence 1917-41) from College Park, items 10020-41 to -64; check the Riverbank papers in the George C. Marshall Foundation Friedman collection for the same monthly reports.
entries.outcome: attempted, open: blocked, the War College Division file 10020-60 is not scanned; only its M912 index card is online (27 Oct 2026, targets/tampico1917/)

entries.title: Communist Party of America underground: book-cipher addresses and names in letters seized at 170 Bleecker St., New York, 1920-21
entries.correspondents: District organizers and members (signing D.O. 5, J. Mortin, Frederick Mayer ...) ↔ the Executive Secretary ("EXSEC", Paul Holt), Communist Party of America
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 65, Investigative Case Files of the Bureau of Investigation 1908-1922, Old German Files (M1085) roll 940, case 202600 ("202600-1775 THRU 202600-1949-1 (4 of 4)", naId 369272950), multi-page PDFs M1085-940A, -940B, -940C ("Copies of Letters & Documents Found at 170 Bleecker St.")
entries.folio_note: OCR count: 77 runs of line/letter fraction groups (e.g. "(New code) 3/3 3/4 2/8 3/7 1/14 - 7/3 2/7 4/4 ...", "Old code P 14 ... 14/15 2/1 6/4"), about 2,400 fraction tokens over the three PDFs. 27 runs are followed by a Bureau "Decode:" or "the above code reads as follows" line; about 50 runs show no decode nearby. 940C also copies the party's own instruction for the system (count lines down, letters across on a set page; a dash between words).
entries.status: Seen in the OCR of the digitised reel: Bureau agents copied the seized letters and decoded many of the coded addresses (class A: decodes in the same file give cribs for the page). The undecoded runs are names, addresses and telegraph covers. Not on DECODE; nothing in the repo. 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #116; targets/cpa1920/, in progress): 28 runs and 439 tokens on the typed pages (the 77 runs / 2,400 tokens of the OCR count also took in dates and ratios); handwritten pages not yet searched. Key grid rebuilt from the Bureau's own decodes of 16 runs; the book is not identified.
entries.why: The early US Communist underground (after the Palmer raids) hid its contact network in a book code; the undecoded runs would name more of that network, and the system is a clean example of a period book cipher.
entries.verify: Open M1085-940A/B/C from the reel record, pair each decoded run with its plaintext to rebuild the key page(s) ("old code" P 14 and the "new code"), then read the runs without a decode; check the other parts of case 202600 on roll 940 for more.

entries.title: Lt. Gen. Richard Taylor (Dept. of Alabama, Mississippi and East Louisiana) → Maury, S. D. Lee, Forrest and others: telegram letter-books with Confederate Vigenère passages copied in cipher only
entries.correspondents: Richard Taylor (by W. F. Bullock Jr., AAG) → D. H. Maury (Mobile), S. D. Lee (Augusta), Wirt Adams, Gov. Clark, Richmond and others
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 109, War Department Collection of Confederate Records, Chapter II vols. 10, 11 and 196 (Telegrams Sent, Department of Alabama, Mississippi and East Louisiana, 1864-1865)
entries.folio_note: Cipher words written in capitals inside the clear copies, word lengths kept. Vol. 196 (Feb-Mar 1865, naId 45485022): about 40 runs, e.g. frame 0061 = p. 117, Taylor → Maury 12 Mar 1865 (viewed). Vol. 11 (1865, naId 12127054): about 10 runs. Vol. 10 (1864-65, naId 16878212): about 8 runs. Run lists with best key per run in research/nara_triage_d/capruns1.txt and capruns2.txt.
entries.status: Not unsolved in the strict sense: the keys are the known Confederate ones. Frame 0061 transcribed from the image and read here with COME RETRIBUTION (Vigenère, key running through the cipher letters only): 'Telegraph in cipher what [cavalry you have on which side of bay, strength and name of commander] ... Direct [cavalry so keep close to enemy] as possible ... [keep in constant telegraphic communication with] Genl D W Adams ... indicate in cipher [what] ... you have decided upon [outside through which to communicate]'. On the OCR alone, runs in vol. 11 read with COME RETRIBUTION ('stores', 'will move westward', 'was evacuated by') and runs in vol. 10 read with COMPLETE VICTORY ('Genl Johnston this alone will restore confidence', 'renders the assignment'). The volumes carry the 'War Records COPIED' stamp, so the Official Records may print these telegrams, but whether OR printed the cipher words deciphered or left them out was not checked. Not on DECODE; known.py: no hit for Come Retribution, Taylor 1865 or Markoe. 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #111; targets/taylor1865/, in progress): four telegrams of 12 and 30 Mar and 6 and 8 Apr 1865 read from the NARA images with COME RETRIBUTION; the 6 and 8 April ones are printed in clear in the OR. Frame 0061's "on each side of bay" and "[?west] point" confirmed.
entries.why: A set of Confederate field ciphers from the last months of the war (Mobile campaign, Wilson's raid) that a known key reads, with the clear sense of each telegram in the same book: a quick, verifiable reading and a test set for Confederate key usage (which key, and when the change was made).
entries.score_note: Scored from NARA OCR and one viewed frame during the Oct 2026 NARA bulk-scan triage (research/nara_triage_d/)
entries.verify: Check OR Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 and vol. 45 pt. 2 for Taylor's telegrams of 12 Mar 1865 to Maury and to S. D. Lee (does OR give the cipher words in clear?). Then transcribe the capital runs from the images of vols. 10, 11 and 196 and decipher with vig.py.
entries.prior_art: Keys known (Manchester Bluff / Complete Victory / Come Retribution); OR not checked (checked 27 Oct 2026: web search for the 12 Mar 1865 Taylor-Maury text gave no hit; Rosenbach Telegraphic History holds Maury-Taylor telegrams of Nov 1864-Feb 1865)

entries.title: Code message carried by Henry Kolbeck and Olga de Visser from Mexico City to San Antonio, seized with its key at Laredo
entries.correspondents: claimed: Hugo Horotwischka (secretary, Austro-Hungarian Legation, Mexico City) → Joe Bolner, San Antonio (self-styled representative of the Central Powers)

entries.folio_note: One message plus key.
entries.status: Cards: the Vissers were arrested at Laredo carrying a message in code and its key, weeks after the Zimmermann telegram. No decipherment is recorded on the card, but with the key held it was probably read. The MID correspondence file itself (RG 165, entry 65, MID 1917-41) is not digitised; only the index card (M1194/M912/M1474) is online. The MID cards are not digitised (27 Oct 2026). 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #108; targets/visser1917/, in progress): the ciphertext and a key strip survive as photostats in BI OG 2889 (M1085 roll 302, frames 39, 42, 58, 59). The text is Spanish, not German. The carriers were the cousins Henry Kolbeck and Olga de (d') Visser, detained at Laredo on 14 Feb 1917 (the 22 Feb date is not checked). Kolbeck confessed in April 1917 that he wrote the document himself (complaint under s. 37 of the Penal Code, May 1917). Read by the Bureau in 1917; that reading is not located.
entries.why: Central Powers courier traffic between Mexico City and Texas in February 1917.

entries.title: Flugabwehrkommando Schwarzwald (Luftgau VII), Funksprüche in the Luftgauschlüssel double transposition, Western campaign 1940
entries.correspondents: Flugabwehrkommando Schwarzwald and its Flak groups/regiments (Luftgaukommando VII, Munich) ↔ subordinate Flak units
entries.place: Black Forest / Upper Rhine (Flak-Gruppe Schwarzwald-Süd and -Nord)
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 242, T405 (German Air Force Records of the Luftgaukommandos, Flak ...), roll 9 (NAID 332033680)
entries.folio_note: c. 70 Funkspruch forms in five-letter groups, frames 863-867 (one message in 5 parts, 'Un 1.Tl-179' ... '5.Tl-204'), 889-901, 917-936, 947-948, 964-1003, 1010-1011, 1025-1056, 1069-1105, 1113 (plus 565, 9); most messages are multi-part ('1.Tl', '2.Tl' ...) of 160-250 letters. Frame 349: an exercise Fernschreiben of 25.2.1939 (221 letters) to Luftverteidigungskommando Berlin; frame 350: its key card 'Annahme: Luftgauschlüssel für den 25.2.1939', two transposition keys a (21) and b (19), Kenngruppen qli vzn fks puc.
entries.status: Not on DECODE, not in the repo (known.py: T405, Schwarzwald, Luftgau: no hits). The letter counts of the groups are those of German plaintext with X as word separator (pooled IC 0.060 on noisy OCR, top letters E R X I N A), so this is a transposition, not Enigma. Tested 27 Oct 2026: the 1939 exercise message reads in full with its key card (double columnar transposition, key a then b, the group containing the Kenngruppe 'fks' at group 7 dropped, CH written Q): 'ROEM X ERSTE FLAKREGIMENT X ZWOELF X RES X FLAKABTEILUNG ... WERDEN IN DER NACHT DURQ TEILE DER X FLAKTRANSPORTABTEILUNG X DREIEINS X NAQ X MAGDEBURG X VERLEGT X LUFTGAUKOMMANDO X ROEM X DREI' (dw1939.py). The 1940 messages carry no key and no decipherment on the frames; some have a typed Fernschreiben in clear on a neighbouring frame (e.g. 862, 4 June 1940) that may be the same text.
entries.why: A large, dated file of German hand-cipher (Doppelwürfel) radio traffic from 1940, with the system and one key proven from the same reel: a ready test bed for double-transposition hill-climbing and possibly cribbed by the clear Fernschreiben filed beside it.
entries.score_note: Scored from NARA OCR during the Oct 2026 NARA bulk-scan triage (research/nara_triage_g/); frames 349-350 and the key verified on the images, the 1940 messages read from OCR only
entries.verify: Transcribe the five-part message of frames 863-867 and two or three same-day messages from the images; match them to the clear Fernschreiben on neighbouring frames (862, 878, 888, 897 ...) as cribs; then run a double-transposition solver with key lengths 15-25 (one daily key per day for all messages).

entries.language: Russian or French (cover text French; plaintext unknown)
entries.shelfmark: NARA, RG 64 (microfilm M1486, Records of the Russian Consulates in the U.S., 1862-1922), roll 83, target 2 "Cables and Coded Communications, 1893-1910" (original: Russian Consulate New York, box 124); file unit naId 571170362
entries.folio_note: Roll 83 frames 0692-1550 (target 2 starts at frame 0692). Ciphertext circulars in 2-digit bigram-key groups: f.0696-0697 (15 Dec 1906), 0698 (10 Mar 1910, No. 63637), 0712 (18 Jun 1902, No. 281), 0732 (1895, No. 4945), 0742-0743 (No. 416), 0749 (1891, No. 3313), 0751-0752 (13 Aug 1891, No. 3902, c. 330 groups, viewed: clean, no interlinear), 0755-0757 (22 Mar 1895, No. 5078), 0769-0770 (10 Mar 1895, No. 5015), 0774 (31 Dec 1904, No. 1201), 0818-0820 (May/Jul 1897, Nos. 5657, 5700), 0823, 0835-0836, 0842, 0847, 0849; the consulate's replies in cipher f.0733-0735 (No. 519, 1895, Olarovsky); 5-digit secret circular No. 864 "aux Ambassades, Légations, Consulats" f.0703-0705 (c. 350 groups, viewed: clean, groups split by hand into 3-figure parts); 5-digit cables f.0694 (cable No. 63, 22 Oct 1908), 0800-0801, 0880-0882 (Oustinoff); naval-ministry letter cipher f.0805-0807 (5-letter groups with a repeating 2849284928... key line and Russian clear text: decrypted). Key material on the same roll: instructions and worked examples for the bigram keys No. 381 (1893; f.0780-0793) and No. 389 (1900; f.0713-0727, with the 12 Dec 1865 "Pesth" example in plaintext, transposition sheet and cipher), circular on key No. 400 (1905; f.0731), additions to the dictionary key No. 402 (1910; f.0728, 0802-0803), lozungi to recipher key No. 448 "Lambda" (1915; f.0869), rules on keeping keys (f.0759-0764), Naval Ministry cipher No. 383 (f.0863-0865) and Naval key No. 394 instructions plus dictionary (f.0884-0900, 0928-1073), and decode tables (f.1088-1550, "Разборная таблица No. 404" f.1443).
entries.status: Found in the RG 64 bulk_all hits (frames with 2-digit groups in a Russian consulate file); full roll OCR read and two frames viewed (0703, 0751). Some circulars carry the consulate's letter-by-letter decipherment worksheets on the following frames (f.0706-0711 after No. 864; 0758, 0772, 0776, 0794-0796, 0822-0825, 0837), so part of the run was read at the time; others show no worksheet in the OCR of the adjacent frames (1891 No. 3902, 1895 Nos. 4945 and 5078, 1906, 1910). The cipher system is described in full on the roll (bigram table + transposition "transparents" Lit. A/B/D; 3-figure values regrouped in 5s for the telegraph), and keys 381/389 come with plaintext-ciphertext examples. Not on DECODE; known.py: no hit for M1486, Olarovsky, Russian Consulate. Not in catalogue.json or any nara_* folder. || Brackx, issue #167 (28 Oct 2026): M1486 roll 83 (target 2, frames 0692-1550): the system is a bigram-table scheme (stencils A and D; instructions to keys 381 and 389, worked example 0790-0792); only key No. 404's tables are filmed (frames 1440-1446), so the 1888-1905 circulars' keys 356, 375, 381, 389 are not filmed; later circulars were deciphered at the time. Not checked on the film here.
entries.why: A run of tsarist Foreign Ministry cipher circulars to a consulate, filed with the consulate's own key instructions and worksheets: rare primary evidence of Russian diplomatic bigram ciphers and naval codes of 1890-1910, and the unread circulars can be tested against keys and worked examples on the same roll.

entries.status: Found in the slice L word-hit triage (agent_59.md) and confirmed from the purport list OCR (fetched 27 Oct 2026). entries.title: James Wilkinson ('Agent 13') ↔ Spanish governors of Louisiana: cipher letters in two dictionary-and-table codes, most pages unread
entries.correspondents: James Wilkinson → Spanish governors of Louisiana / agents of the Spanish Crown (Miró, Carondelet, Gayoso; not itemised in the source), and replies
entries.language: English (some French words in the plaintext)
entries.shelfmark: Library of Congress, Manuscript Division, reproductions of the Archivo General de Indias, Papeles procedentes de Cuba, legajo 2374 (LoC page numbers 1524-1652, 2874-3072; 'File 1', 'File A', 'File B'); originals AGI Cuba leg. 2374
entries.folio_note: Per the Chu/Valenti/Knight project inventory (github c2huc2hu/wilkinson data.txt): about 73 pp of ciphertext without decipherment and 28 pp with interlinear decipherment. Two systems: the '1078' code (table of ~1,240 numbered words with caret, plus page.row dictionary references with one or two bars for the column; dictionary ~780 pp x 2 cols x 29 rows) and a different '1096' system. Unsolved pages: LoC 1524, 1576-1583, 1598-1600, 1630-1631, 1642-1643, 2874, 2888-2890, 2895-2898, 2907-2909, 2930, 2943-2946, 2951-2953, 2962-2965, 2972, 3044-3047; decipherments for 1614-1624 and 1635-1637 exist (LoC 2975-2989, 3014-3018) but the project did not have the scans.
entries.status: Partly read. Chu, Valenti and Knight (EMNLP Findings 2020, arXiv 2010.04746) recovered 75.1% of cipher-word tokens on a held-out 500-token excerpt (LoC 3044-3045) by a known-plaintext wordbank from the deciphered pages plus a neural LM; the dictionary itself was never identified and the 1096 system was not attacked. Not in the repo (known.py: no hits for 2374, Papeles de Cuba, Wilkinson cipher). Not on DECODE as far as checked.
entries.why: Wilkinson's paid espionage for Spain while commanding the US Army is a major early-republic affair; the unread letters would document what he sold and when, including the Burr period.
entries.score_note: Scored from the Chu/Valenti/Knight 2020 paper and their released transcriptions during the Oct 2026 Library of Congress sweep (research/us_loc/); LoC scans not viewed (not online at loc.gov as far as found)
entries.verify: Get the LoC reproductions of AGI Cuba leg. 2374 (or AGI originals via PARES, Papeles de Cuba 2374); identify the dictionary (c. 1790s English dictionary of ~780 pp, 2 cols, 29 rows: candidates Entick's New Spelling Dictionary editions, Johnson abridgements); bank the 27 deciphered-but-unbanked pages; attack the 1096 system from the 1614-1624/2975-2989 pair.
entries.prior_art: partly read: Chu, Valenti & Knight 2020, 75.1% tokens on one excerpt; dictionary unidentified (checked 28 Oct 2026: arXiv paper, GitHub repo, web search; no later full reading found)

entries.title: Philip IV to Juan de Velasco y la Cueva, conde de Siruela, ambassador in Genoa: despatch entirely in cipher (PARES title "Minuta de despacho cifrada")
entries.correspondents: Philip IV → conde de Siruela (Genoa)
entries.shelfmark: AGS, EST,LEG,3594,312
entries.folio_note: 4 images online; 3⅓ pages, entirely in cipher except the address; signed "Yo el Rey"
entries.status: Swept 28 Oct 2026 (Brice Dudout's PARES sweep, facet filter idFI); "cifrada", 17th century: "Minuta de despacho cifrada a Juan de Velasco y la Cueva, conde de Siruela". Images viewed: 3 pages of symbol cipher with short clear passages, signed "Yo el Rey"; no decipherment visible. Sibling of the Genoa 1638-51 row already in the catalogue (Velasco y la Cueva, Eraso…), which may give the key family. Corrected 28 Oct 2026 after a full transcription (64 lines, 1,818 tokens): not a minute with clear passages but a despatch entirely in cipher (only the address in clear), dated 20 Nov 1638, in the Genoa 1638 system (genes1638 key family) with extra chancery signs (ℰ, ꝓ, ʒ, underlined sigla). Key K3k, trained on declared pairs in the same chancery hand (3594,149↔148, 158↔157, 160↔159, 151↔150 pp. 1-2, 3595,308↔309), frozen, then tested on 3594,151 image 3 ↔ 150 never seen: 0.888 of characters / 0.812 of words (normalised spelling; 200 controls p99 0.313 / 0.161), validated. Reading of 312: 884 words, about 87-88 % read by sense (61 unresolved, 57 restored, 8 probable), below the 95 % rule; what remains is the nomenclator (44 codes), not the signs. Subject: the negotiation with Genoa (passes, exchange of prisoners, galleys), answering Siruela's letters of 4 and 20 Oct 1638. Reported by Brice Dudout from his own look at the images; not yet checked here.
entries.why: A royal despatch to Genoa entirely in cipher, probably never deciphered in print; the key family is known (genes1638), so a full reading looks within reach.
entries.score_note: Images viewed (all 4) and fully transcribed by Brice Dudout's agents; key validated, reading about 87-88 %, not yet at 95 %.
entries.verify: The nomenclator codes (44 unresolved): the sent original or a plain copy in Genoa, or other royal despatches to Siruela in the same hand.

entries.title: Riverbank Laboratories 'Mexican codes' and unsorted cryptographic papers (the surviving Riverbank Department of Ciphers files)
entries.correspondents: Mexican government / agents (intercepted) -> Riverbank Department of Ciphers (W. F. and E. S. Friedman) for the State, War, Navy and Justice Departments
entries.shelfmark: New York Public Library, Manuscripts and Archives Division, MssCol 176 (Bacon cipher collection), box 15 'Riverbank Labs -- student exercises and lessons, Mexican codes' and box 16 'Riverbank Labs -- unsorted material concerning cryptography'
entries.folio_note: Box-level description only (1982 accession sheet, 33 boxes). Not digitised (NYPL Digital Collections shows 10 Baconian items only). Contents unknown: could be worksheets, intercept copies or training exercises built from them.
entries.status: Friedman's own accounts (NSA Friedman papers, folders 433/513) say Riverbank worked codes and ciphers forwarded by State, War, Navy and Justice in 1916-20; a 1917 Army note quoted in a web search summary says the main work was Mexican messages (source PDF not opened). Friedman wrote in 1948 that the Riverbank cipher records were thought destroyed after Fabyan's death (Cora Tyzzer letter, NSA A69876) and that the LoC Fabyan collection held none of them; the NYPL boxes came via Fabyan's widow to George Curtis (gift 1960), so these two boxes may be the only survivors. MI-8 broke several Mexican government codes in 1917-19 (repo: research/nara_triage_c/e), so many messages will be read; whether any are unread is unknown. Schmeh (2018) saw three boxes, not these. NSA historians (Dave Hatch and a colleague, a November visit, year not given) went through all nine Riverbank boxes and found them 'very duplicative and mixed': page proofs of Riverbank publications, student folders and exercises on graph paper, a few Parker Hitt letters; no cipher intercepts are mentioned (NSA blog 'A great TDY', Doc ID 6919113, released 30 Mar 2026).
entries.why: The only known surviving working files of the first US government cryptanalytic unit (Riverbank 1917-18); any message they hold unread is WWI German-Mexican traffic.
entries.score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 Riverbank sweep (research/chi_riverbank/); not viewed
